description.text: A light, strong bolt constructed to meet Bolt Council specifications. Each bolt is guaranteed to contain enough aluminum to make eight square yards of weapon-grade aluminum foil.
Crafted of aluminum, this bolt will give anyone an unpleasant sting with its nasty barbs. Each bolt is guaranteed to contain enough aluminum to make eight square yards of weapon-grade aluminum foil.

A cruel and crafty mind was behind the manufacture of these wickedly barbed aluminum bolts. Each bolt is guaranteed to contain enough aluminum to make eight square yards of weapon-grade aluminum foil.

This bolt is sure to give your enemy the ol' hot-foot. Or, at least, the ol' stab-foot.
Designed by an indecisive boltsmith, this bolt houses an additional bolt inside the bolt's shaft. Shooting it into an enemy's face is the quickest way to pop the latch and extract the hidden bolt.

A thoroughly unpleasant bolt that steals some of the target's life energy, and, for a nominal soul tax, passes it on to the crossbow wielder. Due to certain clauses in the necromantic contract only animals are subject to the unnatural energies in this bolt.

The hot stays hot, and the cool stays cool, thanks to a thick layer of expanded polystyrene foam between the two sides of the bolt head. Stock up before the Bolt Council phases them out due to pressures from environmental groups!
The perfect way to displace any lingering shame, depression, sociopathic tendencies, anxiety, ennui, or just plain old leprosy.
You've stoppered Deth! You then attached Deth to a bolt. It's a little surprising that he (or she) isn't angrier about that, all things considered.

There is a fifth dimension beyond that which is known to Diggles. It is the middle ground between light and shadow, between science and other forms of witchery, and it lies between the pit of man's fears and the summit of his knowledge. This is the dimension of imagination. It is an arrow which we call the Twilight Bolt.
'These are the the cries of the carrots, the cries of the carrots' raved the tuber-despising boltsmith, surveying the destruction wrought by his wicked creation.
This bolt was designed to more efficiently take down erratically behaving constructs. Number five won't be alive for long.
A thick piece of polystyrene foam keeps the two sides of this bolthead separated. This is a good thing, as their constant debates over politics and religion irritate the other bolts in your quiver.
This light, accurate crossbow almost always rocks the sure shot, cause you can't, you won't and you don't stop. Firing bolts, that is.
The construction of this crossbow would not have been possible without generous assistance from one of the kingdom's few snake orthodontists.
